chapter: Road life, segregation and band pranks
title: Willie Smith's constant reading and his cigarette ritual
summary: Crawford describes Willie Smith always reading and saying a prayer before handing over a cigarette.

story.theme_name: Drink, drugs and the bandstand's casualties
story.community_name: Drugs and drink on the bandstand and the road

blocks.x: Were the guys in those periods -- did they read much? I don't mean music, but did many of the guys --
He read a lot of books and stuff?

Always, always reading. He was a peculiar person. He was from Charleston, South Carolina, so he'd be sitting there, reading, smoking a cigarette, always had a book in front of him, always, when he was walking the streets, always was reading. He had a bottle of whisky. And so -- didn't read much. I taught myself how to read more like periodicals, newspapers, books and et cetera, recently. And -- but Willie Smith always had a book. And so,

you'd go by and you'd say, hey, Willie, excuse me a minute. Now, you're interrupting him from reading. Will you give me a cigarette, please? You weren't doing to be -- for no joke. I wanted a cigarette.

So Willie while reading just slip in his pockets and hand me -- no, first he would take out a cigarette, take the cigarette out and take the pack and lay it over, like that. And Willie would say a prayer to himself, first, before he gave me that cigarette. And he'd hand you the cigarette. And I was wondering what that was all about, and never did know, even today, even though Willie's dead. I didn't know what that prayer business -- well, he's a Greek, that's all.
So that was his way of doing things. He'd always lay that cigarette on that pack and then say a prayer. Then he'd take that cigarette and then give it to me. I didn't know.
